conflicts: Lifetime of the 27135.695 cm^-1 (9P3) level: the Battles thesis lists 10.98 ns for the "368 nm transition", which is just 1/A of the single 368 nm line (NIST A = 9.1e7 s^-1); the NIST A values of the 368 nm and 371 nm lines together imply an upper-level lifetime of at most 5.5 ns. The thesis number is not entered.

Lifetimes 10.8 ns (22334.508) and 13.7 ns (22563.824), second-hand from Den Hartog et al. 2011, are much shorter than 1/A of the single NIST-listed line from each level (26 ns and 33 ns): either the NIST A values (old, accuracy not rated) are too small or other strong branches exist. Not resolved.

743.014 nm line: the 157Gd isotope shift 486(65) MHz does not follow the sequence of the other isotopes; the authors report a King-plot nonlinearity but also say the 157Gd hyperfine structure was not fully resolved.
Isotope abundances: NIST composition table (entered) vs the slightly different values printed by Chavarría-Sibaja et al. (154Gd 2.15%, 155Gd 14.73%, 157Gd 15.68%, 158Gd 24.87%, 160Gd 21.90%).
not_found: Lifetimes of 15 of the 17 drawn excited levels (22820.895, 23103.66, 23389.782, 24430.425, 24849.514, 24854.297, 25043.649, 25376.313, 25661.34, 27135.695, 27425.245, ...): the measurements exist (Den Hartog, Bilty, Lawler, J. Phys. B 44, 055001 (2011), 136 levels, ±5%; Xu, Jiang, Svanberg, J. Phys. B 36, 411 (2003); Wang et al., J. Phys. B 46, 045003 (2013); Marek & Stahnke, Z. Phys. A 298, 81 (1980)) but all are paywalled / captcha-blocked and no deposit (Figshare, arXiv, OSTI full text, Internet Archive) was found; only abstracts were read.

Experimental transition probabilities with uncertainties (Lawler, Bilty, Den Hartog, J. Phys. B 44, 095001 (2011), 1290 Gd I lines): paywalled, not opened; NIST A values on the site are older, unrated ones.

Ground-term 4f7 5d 6s2 9D°J hyperfine constants of 155Gd and 157Gd from the original magnetic-resonance work (Unsworth, J. Phys. B 2, 122 (1969)) and the J-dependent isotope shifts / hyperfine constants of the 4f7 5d 6s6p 9D and 9F levels (Jin et al., Phys. Rev. A 42, 1416 (1990); Blaum et al., Eur. Phys. J. D (2000), doi:10.1007/s100530070103): paywalled, only abstracts read. Only the 9D°2 constants are entered, second-hand and unsigned.

Isotope shifts and hyperfine constants for the drawn 368-452 nm lines: not found in an openable source (Blaum et al. 2000 cover the 422-429 nm 9D°J - 9F(J+1) lines; Niki et al. 2005 the blue diode-laser lines).
Precise absolute transition frequencies (frequency-comb or wavemeter based): none found for Gd I.
Laser cooling or trapping of Gd: no experimental demonstration found; only a thesis-level proposal (368 nm, 423 nm) and a Zeeman-slower test with a broadband diode laser.
Level 34586 cm^-1 (J = 1) of the LLNL photoionization scheme (lifetime 820 ns; 581.037 nm step with A = 2.305e5 s^-1) is not in the NIST level list used by the site and was not entered.
notes: Stable isotopes: 155Gd and 157Gd have I = 3/2 (both nuclear moments negative: mu = -0.2591 and -0.3398 nuclear magnetons in the IAEA table); the others have I = 0. Hyperfine convention: E = A K/2 + B [3K(K+1) - 4I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [8I(2I-1)J(2J-1)], K = F(F+1)-J(J+1)-I(I+1) (as printed by Adhikari et al.). The LLNL constants (ground level 9D°2, 17380.827 level, 575.19 nm line) are modeling inputs printed without signs or uncertainties in a table that exists only as an image (read from the rendered PDF page); treat them as indicative. Isotope-shift keys "A-B" mean nu(A) - nu(B). This file is thin because the two key Wisconsin papers (lifetimes and transition probabilities, 2011) could not be opened. Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: top-level ionization_limit; transition field use_source.
